tags: why do dogs paw at you
script: That little paw tap on your leg or arm is your dog's version of tapping you on the shoulder. Puppies start pawing at their mother's belly to encourage milk flow, and that instinct carries into adulthood as a general attention-seeking gesture. When your dog paws at you, they've usually learned it works, it gets you to look at them, talk to them, or give them what they want, whether that's food, a walk, or just a scratch behind the ears. It's also a sign of trust. Dogs generally don't paw at people or animals they feel uneasy around. So that paw isn't random, it's a learned communication tool that works.
